newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU agrees tougher stance on Cuba.
newsitem.headline: EU agrees tougher stance on Cuba.

text.p: The European Union on Monday agreed to a tougher stance towards Cuba and vowed to pressure the country to respect human rights, free speech and freedom of association.
The new policy -- the details of which were agreed last week -- was rubber stamped without further discussion at a meeting of EU finance ministers.
The change of direction comes as Cuba accuses EU member Spain of meddling in its affairs and has withdrawn official approval for a new Spanish ambassador.

Under the new strategy, the 15-nation Union will seek opportunities, both public and privately, of reminding the Cuban authorities of their "fundamental responsibilities on human rights, in particular freedom of speech and association."
The EU also also intends to intensify talks with the Cuban authorities, and with all sectors of society, "to promote respect for human rights and real progress towards pluralist democracy".

European Union leaders have been under pressure from the United States to strengthen their stance towards Havana, which Washington hit with tougher economic sanctions this year after two U.S. civilian aircraft were shot down by Cuba in March.

The United States and the European Union have repeatedly clashed on Cuba policy since the aircraft were downed, with Washington passing laws intended to punish foreign investors who "traffic" with nationalised properties on the island.
Under the Helms-Burton law, named for its sponsors, top executives and major shareholders of firms found to be "trafficking" are to be barred from the United States.
The U.S. says its citizens never received compensation for assets seized by Cuban President Fidel Castro since 1959, so it treats them as stolen properties.
The EU policy change makes clear its position on Helms-Burton remains unchanged.
